findings.text: after_suite.log_path names arms.log, which is a single file holding a full-text arm per comparison (AFTER arm at lines 3-8, BASE arm at lines 10-62). The reviewed change's real head arm is the AFTER arm (69 passed, EXIT=0, no failures), but because the BASE arm's two test_render_receipt_paths.py failures are printed in the same file, reckon's mechanical derivation (review.py added_failures_from_gate_logs, called on read via annotate_review_of_run) takes them as head failures and computes added_failure_count 2, capping the review total at ADDED_FAILURES_TOTAL_CAP=5. The honest count is 0. A per-arm log (or an after-only extraction) removes the hazard; the manifest should name one.

baseline_suite records completed:true and failure_ids for the two scratch-scaffold failures, but the log it names (baseline-arm.log) is not the arm that produced them: it ends '.......F.F.FTerminated' then 'EXIT=143' with no pytest summary, so it is an unreadable terminated run. The readable base arm is the BASE section of arms.log (2 failed, 58 passed, 22 skipped, EXIT=1). A manifest that names an unreadable log for a completed arm cannot support its own completed:true.

§2's surface accounting describes the relativize subcommand as also having a --check mode that reads the files staged for commit and exits nonzero, naming each non-exempt offender, and names worktree_path_offenders as the predicate the commit check and the repository test share. At head the subcommand has only the in-place apply mode (no --check), and worktree_path_offenders has no production consumer — only tests/test_filepath.py:259 and docs. The node's report defers --check to §4 ('--check is not added (it belongs to the §4 guard node)'); that is a defensible split, but §2's own paragraph states the mode as part of the command surface and §2's done-when does not name it, so the ownership is ambiguous and a coordinator should settle it before §4.

The landing fragment says docs/evidence/archive/figure-and-solver-audit-landed.html carries 'a path split by a line wrap'. That source line (996 at head) is a single line: the span is broken by a literal space after 's19-northstar/' (an HTML source artifact), not by a newline. The function leaves it unmapped because the layout is space-broken/incomplete, not because of a line wrap; the outcome (report and leave) is correct but the stated reason is inaccurate.

justifications.goal_fidelity: §2's core deliverable is delivered and independently re-derived: one rule owner (relativize_worktree_paths) + one predicate (worktree_path_offenders) + two module constants in nova/database/filepath.py, repository_relative delegating its worktree case to the same matcher, and a relativize subcommand on the existing filepath click group (nova/database/scripts.py:33). I applied the function to every one of the 1,147 tracked files the census names: 65 are launch scripts (.sh/.sbatch/.py) deferred to §3, 1,077 data files are clean, and exactly 5 data files retain the pattern with spans the function returns unmapped (9 spans). The arithmetic reconciles with the plan: 1,082 data files carried the pattern at base f9940c575, 1,079 were rewritten (997da31d1, 4,457 insertions == 4,457 deletions), 3 carried only an unmappable mention. justifications.reuse: No new machinery: the work extends the existing nova/database/filepath.py and the existing filepath click group, and reuses the lexical approach the plan cites from reckon's _rewrite_worktree_roots without importing it. The tests extend the existing tests/test_filepath.py rather than a new file.
justifications.scope_discipline: The reviewed range ce26c583b^..ec1a51c36 touches exactly three .py files (nova/database/filepath.py, nova/database/scripts.py, tests/test_filepath.py), 1,079 data files and one landing fragment. No plan file is edited, and no .sh/.sbatch/.png/.svg changes anywhere in the range (grep count 0), matching §2's 'No launch script, PNG or SVG changes, and no solve runs'. The three .py paths and the fragment are all inside the manifest's declared write paths.

limitations: The baseline/after suites the reviewed manifest names were not re-run by this review (they are login-node pytest runs over the whole repo; re-running contends with peers). The AFTER arm (69 passed EXIT=0) is read from arms.log, and the mechanical gate that matters (check_reapply.py) was independently reproduced.

The 5 residual data files each carry a span the rule cannot model while keeping the same-bytes/same-line-endings promise: cpu-compile-abort-landed.html is truncated to the project directory, figure-and-solver-audit-landed.html is space-broken after s19-northstar/, the two fsa fragments and thin-interfaces.md mention the bare root as a prose subject. Rewording them (not rewriting) is §3's, per the node's report.
worktree_path_offenders and the relativize --check mode have no production consumer at head; the §4 hook is where they are wired.
